As it was physically impossible for us to get ourselves into our new room with all of our baby’s gear and no elevator we simply went directly to the front desk and waited to request a room change.  The same individual who was checking in our group on the first floor ended up serving us at the front desk (by the time we cleared that line-up) and somehow found us a room right away.  We were happy with the location of our room (1019), it was convenient and close to the elevator and main areas, pool, gardens etc.  It had a garden view but as it turns out most of the rooms do not have ocean views so we were fine with the room.   When we arrived we had to wait quite a while for our bags even though it was already 8pm by the time we got into our room.  As we had missed dinner service we decided to order room service.  The room service menu is VERY limited, and after 11pm it becomes even more limited, also apparently room service costs $5 a pop as does having your mini-fridge restocked.  We ordered a burger, the fish of the day, a pizza and the chocolate cake.  The fish of the day was salmon and it was really delicious but the portion size was miniscule, I would typically eat three times as much as what they gave (I am an average sized woman)  My husband liked the burger but the pizza was disgusting.  Cheese at this resort does not resemble Canadian or American style cheeses so do not expect to eat any great pizza or Mexican etc. while on this vacation.  Speaking of Mexican, the brochure says they have a Mexican buffet called Agave which I was really looking forward to since Mexican food is my favourite. After 4 days of watching for this buffet, I called the concierge and asked where I could find it and was told he didn’t know what I was talking about.  When I referred him to the brochure he said that sometimes they carry Mexican items on the main buffet and that’s when they call it Agave???  What???

Breakfast at the Naos buffet has a lot of variety; the fresh omelettes especially received good reviews.  I liked the French toast with Banana jam and some of the Dominican items such as pumpkin puree and mashed plantains with onions. There were great meat varieties and lots of fresh fruit and a nice juice and smoothie bar (located just outside the buffet on the right – a lot of people missed it).  The service in the main buffet restaurant at breakfast and lunch is terrible.  We were seated and then never saw a server again for the first 3 days. We thought there was no drink service in the buffet until we noticed some people were getting juice from a waiter.  We found out on the 4th day that you can get good service (excellent actually) if you sit in the covered chair area of the restaurant on the far left-hand side of the buffet.  We were finally able to start paying tips when we sat over there.  As always, we brought $300 in tip money and were really looking forward to handing it out but we came home with almost half of it because we simply couldn’t find enough people doing a decent job to tip. 
The lunch buffet has some great items but a lot of really boring or inedible items as well.  The main buffet is called Naos.  They had different items on the buffet every day and some were really good, some were very boring. The cold salads were quite tasty and the sandwich making area was great.  The worst is the fish – I love fish but it was always really slimy, even though they had a different fish dish on the buffet every day it was always mushy.  The only fish I suggest eating on the buffet is whatever is being grilled for you individually.  There are only 2 places to eat lunch, Naos and The Market Grill buffet which has hamburgers, chicken, hot dogs etc.  This place is also the only place you can get tortilla chips and guacamole and pico de gallo which are yummy but if they run out of guac early in the lunch service they don’t make more, even if you beg .   The worst parts of the food are the lack of snacking options and the very mediocre if not inedible desserts.  I am NOT a picky eater, I like food, I have a sweet tooth and I love trying new things but I found myself hungry there quite a bit because they didn’t really have anything that was appetizing between main meals.  You had no real snack options and the desserts were really very bland – there seemed to be no sugar in many of them – I tried a lot and only liked the lemon meringue squares and the chocolate tart from the Gabi Beach – other than this one item, all other chocolate desserts are inedible, like dry sandpaper.  All of the other desserts were beyond bland and the serving sizes were again very tiny – like about 1 inch in diameter for a slice of pie or cake.    This place would benefit from a decent snack bar, even if you had to pay extra for it like they make you pay for the better meals at dinner (every restaurant has items you can pay more for at dinner, ranging from $20 to $50 more per meal which I found really odd for a 5 star all-inclusive)
For dinner, do not do the Buffet – it’s way too much like the lunch buffet and you will quickly get sick of it.  Even the special Dominican night buffet is highly disappointing.  Also do not eat at the Gabi Club at the reserve (different from Gabi Beach which is delicious) Gabi club is just a boring buffet only smaller and more difficult to navigate than the lunch buffet.  We were bumped to Gabi Club for my birthday even though we had a reservation at Aqua.  There was nothing at all special at Gabi Club; it was just the same old lunch buffet in a different building.  They served Roast turkey with no gravy or sauce or cranberries, just dry turkey – SO disappointing! On a positive note, they were kind enough to sing to me in 3 different languages on my birthday and brought cheesecake and the service here was better.
As for good food – The Gabi Beach was delicious – it costs extra but we had the lobster and steaks and it was terrific.  We also loved our meal at Mizu (teppanyaki at the reserve) the salmon and beef were outstanding and the chicken was good too.  They serve sushi as an appetizer which was good but steer clear of the tempura vegetables – inedible soggy grease fritters is what I would call them – definitely in need of improvement.  We were irritated that we had a 6:45 reservation at Mizu and we arrived on time but we were not seated until 7:30 and were not served until after 7:45.  It seems that they wait until the full teppanyaki area is full before they serve you.  We were a party of 4 so we had to wait for another 6 people to come to the restaurant before we could be fed….  Aqua had great service and delicious gourmet food (especially the mushroom pasta and the scallop appetizer) but the portions were very small so be sure to order an appetizer AND pasta AND a main meal if you want to not be hungry.  You may even want to order 2 of something.  Another great meal was had at the Market Grill – the filet mignon was the best beef in the place and the salmon was perfection.  Our server – Anthony Diffo also went above and beyond to get us drinks we ordered even though the ingredients were not available at that bar, he went to another bar to get them – he got a great tip!

Overall positives were the beautiful buildings, nice room, very comfortable bed, gorgeous landscaping (the best I’ve seen anywhere), wildlife (flamingos, storks, ducklings, fish, lizards) plentiful beach beds and lounge chairs, huge pool, entertaining pool bar server (Ramon Fuego was very funny).  Caring and sweet service from Gloria at the pool bar –the best service we got all week.  After she met us on our 3rd day she would look for us every day in a pool bed and bring us different drinks she thought we would like (non-alcoholic for me with my baby) and plantain chips- she also earned decent tips from us.  They had a really yummy coffee bar that served frozen coffee across the bridge over the pool but several times it was unmanned and the cups were locked away so we couldn’t get the frozen coffee.  This should be self-serve in my opinion.  The beach was very beautiful but the water was murky on our visit and had a lot of seaweed.  I did not observe anyone cleaning the seaweed on the beach which seems to be standard practice at the other resorts I’ve visited. 
One day we returned to our room to find a note on our bed (on letterhead typed in 5 languages) that said they found our safe open and had notified management.  I also heard that 2 other people in our group had received the same note and 2 others had returned to their rooms to find their doors ajar.  What’s odd about the note is that I had used the safe myself to tip housekeeping when I returned to the room and found them in there, I opened the safe, tipped the maid and then closed the safe myself and double checked it since she was in our room at the time.  The odd thing is that the safe is located in a closet with a door on it and the closet does not have anything in it that housekeeping would be touching.  Why would they even be in my closet to notice that the safe was open??  Nothing seemed to be missing but I worried about my credit card numbers and cancelled them when I got home just to be safe.
Make sure you bring enough small bills for tipping because it seems like any good service does depend on tips and the front desk will not make change for you for more than about $5 or $10.      
You would also benefit from a Spanish translator like the iPhone and blackberry apps my husband and I downloaded because very few people here speak English and those that claim to speak English seem to lack comprehension (a complaint about a suite door being left ajar by housekeeping was responded to with “well you do understand that we have to clean your room”).  We had to request things in Spanish a couple of times to get what we needed.  A lot of the guest here spoke spanish and I realize this is a spanish speaking country but we've been to other spanish speaking destinations (mexico, belize, honduras) and never had so much trouble communicating before.
If you actually took the time to read this whole review I hope it helps.  We had a relaxing time at the very beautiful and well appointed Paradisus Palma Real with our baby but would look elsewhere next time for consistent service that meets our expectations and food that keeps us satisfied.

reviews.author: jadams1992
reviews.title: Full Capacity felt we had it to ourselves!
reviews.text:
We just had an incentive program at the Paradisus and while the hotel was full, the beaches and pool areas seemed wide open.
Food service was great at restaurants and the buffett was on par with any of the other upper scale all-inclusives in Punta Cana.
Aded highlights, we enjoyed the enteratinment at night and a host of activities during the day!

reviews.author: Karla R
reviews.title: Great! but not for business...
reviews.text:
The hotel is gorgoeus, the beach is amazing, the people serving in the hotel are great, food is awesome, activities are well organized, rooms are so comfortable.
This is a great place for a vacation!
if you want it for business, well, it is not that good becuase the wireless network is really bad, they do not have a good solution.
Karla.

reviews.author: Redbudian
reviews.title: Beautiful resort - worth the trip.
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here sort of as a mixed business and pleasure trip.  First of all, the resort itself, from an aesthetic standpoint is gorgeous!  The gardens are well-manicured, the beaches are clean and the hotel works hard to keep the property in great shape.  We were booked under Royal Service, so we did expect a little more service, but the service was hit or miss.  For starters, there is a big language barrier in the Royal Service Lounge/Desk, which is surprising considering the fact that are a lot of American and Brits at the hotel.  Ironically, the people in other part of the hotel spoke English o.k.  Our room had issues with the A/C, so the desk switched us to another room, but apparently the also downgraded us in the process.  The room attendant was missing in action pretty much the entire week, but it wasn't really that big a deal.  The pool, beach, and the lounge (internet, coffee, snacks, etc...) were all worth the upgrade.  Francisco was our waiter on the beach and he was outstanding.  As far as the food goes, it was not great, but they are catering to so many different nationalities it would be hard to please everyone (plus they are serving more local cuisine than anything. The rooms were nice, but the bathroom situation has zero privacy, just as the previous reviews have stated.  The bed is very comfortable. One thing to note it that they are very stingy with towels and washcloths - start asking for them early.  Our meals in the restaurants tended to be worse than in the main cafe.  The Reserve was the only exception, as we did not have a bad meal over there..  There were some places that we could not get in at all like the Sushi restaurant, so make your reservations early.  One negative that we did hear from several people in our large group was that they thought the drinks were watered down.  The Royal Service area by the pool/beach was the exception.  The night we arrived one member of our group actually witnessed the bartenders at the lobby bar pretending to pour from empty bottles.  Other that that one time, it was fine.  The excursions were fun.  Two trips we recommend are the Catamaran where you swim with Sharks and Dolphins and the horse back riding on the beach,   My husband, who is an avid scuba diver and has been all over the Caribbean, Mexico, etc.., said the reefs on the Leeward side of the island were some of the best he's seen. Lastly, the spa was one of the BEST spa treatment I have ever had (and I have been all over the world). If you are into spa treatments then this is the place to go.  No pressure to buy skin or body car products here either.   All in all it was a good stay.  We recommend to anyone.

reviews.author: Gabi L
reviews.title: EXCELENTE HOTEL Y SERVICIO
reviews.text: Estuve ahí para una Convensión de mi trabajo y todo estuvo excelente! Las instalaciones muy buenas en todos los aspectos, limpieza, seguridad, ambiente, etc, y el servicio fue excelente de todo el personal, desde el GM hasta cualquier empleado con el que tuve contacto. El Royal Service maravilloso, sobre todo cuando tuvimos oportunidad de ir a la playa. En general, lo recumiendo ampliamente!!

reviews.author: Gail P
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real
reviews.text: We stayed in their Royal Service and it was just that ROYAL.  The property is beautiful, the food was devine and the service was royal.  We spent our time between the beautiful white sand beach and the Royal Service private pool.  Francisco Gil, Francisco Cabrera & Pedro Cedan were our pool attendents and they were superb.  Liliana de Leon the hostess at Gabi Beach was also great.  We ate 4 out of our 6 nights at Gabi Beach.  Besides the food being wonderful the ambiance at this beach front restaurant was special.  In the evenings the whole resort was lit by candales making the place magical.

reviews.author: hitdaice
reviews.title: Paradisus Experience
reviews.text: The resort complex is amazing. Feels like being in Paradise: sun, beach, rooms, meals, nature! So, the name "Paradisus" is not accidental. This time (December) is quiet enough, you meet there people who came to rest. Still, they have great entertainment, do different shows, themed evenings, live music, and - of course - latin dances. A word must be said about Activities team. Those four guys (Eliezer, Gabriel, Jose, Jimmy) are really good in making your stay much more pleasant and memorable. Generally, staff is very friendly. The one thing you should be aware of is Dominican tranquillity, sometimes with timelessness. But rest must be rest, total escape from the world! Thus, go Paradisus and enjoy!

reviews.author: Vicente Jose R
reviews.title: Perfecto para Trabajo y Vacaciones
reviews.text: Excelente ambiente. Jardines muy cuidados. El personal tiene muy buena actitud.

reviews.author: MonicaR13
reviews.title: Excelent Event !
reviews.text:
We had an event last week , service was excelent the entertainers were very good, they did a BEach Olimpic games it was fun !  thanks to Gabriel, Santa, Angel, Max, Eliezer. Great job !!!
My host was Clevens and I wanted to extend my gratitud for his excelent job !
thanks to all
Monica

reviews.author: KaOs L
reviews.title: Un Paraíso
reviews.text: Un lugar excepcional. Recomendable sin ningún tipo de objeción. La calidad esta a la vista en cada detalle. Hay que remarcar la amabilidad y calidez de todo el personal.

reviews.author: FSP010
reviews.title: PARADISUS lives up to its name - Truly Paradise!
reviews.text: In planning a BUSINESS EVENT, we found Paradise from the Royal Service greating, to the impecible rooms, gourmet dining and the exquisite surroundings.... our business team will be surrounded by paradise as we begin our new year in Janauary!

reviews.author: agostina C
reviews.title: EXPERIENCIA INOLVIDABLE
reviews.text:
En el mes de Octubre y  primeros días estuvimos junto con un grupo de agentes de viajes y nos alojamos en este Hotel. Todo es un Lujo! la decoración que tiene el Hotel, junto con todas las aereas, the reserve, son hermosas, super de moda, de muy buen gusto. 
El spa que poseen es divino, las habitacione super amplias, lo mismo que el baño, muy bueno el detalle de la puertita de madera que separa la habitacion con el baño.
Pileta hermosa, super amplia, el sector de la playa que tienen tambien.
La gastronomia es buena, Muy buen desayuno!! la panaderia es para destacar, y el Restaurante Pasion es hermoso, comida muy rica.
Los animadores Angel, Gabriel, Santa yt Eliezer, Fueron re buenos, nos enseñaron a  bailar bachata, salsa, jugar al voley, super animada la fiesta de haloween.
Sueño con poder volver

reviews.author: CMStendhal
reviews.title: Bad experience,poor service to costumers.
reviews.text: I arrived today, November 2nd. 2011. First surprise, a lizard was waiting for us on the bed. Later I asked for a feather pillow, a simple request that was an impossible task. The hotel has them, but I was told that they were not available for our room category! We are paying 300 dlls per night and come with a convention of 200 people, I went to the reception desk and asked to speak with the manager, another impossible task. Everything here seems to be very complicated. The guest services guy told me that he needed to be in good terms with his boss, not with the guests at the hotel. the safe wasn't working, we reported it and told them we needed it fixed before dinner. We waited for more than an hour, and after calling several times we finally had it fixed and, of course, were late for dinner. I still haven't got my pillow and its already midnight. This hotel is supposed to be a luxury resort, but it is really dissapointing and except for one guy who attended my call at reception at 11pm, people are rude. I will never come back again.

reviews.author: ChiliD9
reviews.title: Beautiful property, experience so-so
reviews.text:
I have stayed at a number of properties throughout the Carribean and Mexico and thought this was definitely subpar, based on my prior experiences.  The hotel property is beautifully maintained, on a picturesque beach (I'll take into consideration that the large amount of seaweed that had driften onshore was a fluke, from a hurricane).  The hotel room I stayed in was very roomy and comfortable.
The main complaints I had with this property was the food and drinks.  During the day, there were essentially two places where you could find breakfast or lunch.  Not too many options to choose from, and the selection didn't really change.  At the bars, you could only get one brand of beer and the liquors were local Dominican brands.  The bartender at the pool was very entertaining, but didn't make the drinks taste any better.
We also had a couple group events and felt extremely uncomfortable from a temperature perspective.  It seemed like the only place you could get A/C was in your room.
Lastly, it was difficult getting a reservation at the restaurants in the evening, unless you planned ahead at least a day.  It was strange that you would walk bye the restaurant that night and it wouldn't seem very busy, but they couldn't get you in.  Also, the staff was not very competent in English.  On multiple occasions, we had to get someone over to help translate our orders at meals.

reviews.author: ScottyA320
reviews.title: Great Resort for leisure or business
reviews.text:
I've stayed at a lot of places in the Dominican Republic including the best chain Hotels such as Marriott and Hilton; this is every bit as good and what makes it better is a combination of accommodations and the genuine customer service offered by the staff here.
I have stayed in both the suites and standard rooms here in my past visits; both are very spacious and beautiful and the beds are outstanding!!!
There is quite a selection of restaurants to chose from here serving anything from international buffet/grilled to order food to specialty restaurants serving french cuisine (very good!)  Japanese Hibachi - similar to Benny Hanna's. There are quite a few more; dress code for these restaurants range from resort casual (shorts T shirt and flip flops) to Resort elegant; long pants and long sleeve button down shirts for men and dresses for ladies. 
If you drink, all the bars (which is part of the all inclusive plan) serve only top shelf alcohol (unlike other resorts); I'd strongly suggest going to see David at the main bar/lounge in the evenings which is across from the reception desk - he makes outstanding drinks; especially Mojitos!  His very high spirited personality compliments his work :-)
The beaches here are the cleanest and most orderly which I have seen up and down the coast.  Since I've only been here for work, I really can't expound further on the activities - they look fun though "and safe."  The crowd here is a combination of newly weds on their honeymoons, Families with children and an occasional person on business like myself. The majority which come to visit the Paradisus come from all over Latin America, Europe and the US.  The feeling here:  Peaceful, warm and happy!
The only draw back I encountered is wireless signal for computers/PDAs can be hit or miss in the rooms.  Wireless is strong in the common areas such as the lounge and business centers also... bring Mosquito repellant (lots of mosquitoes at night) toiletries to cover your stay. Their shop here does sell these items but are ridiculously expensive ex: a small aerosol can of mosquito repellant will cost you $15.00!

reviews.author: JustECOSM
reviews.title: Keep your expectations low
reviews.text: This is a very large (maybe too large) property that looks good when you arrive. The lobby is spacious and attractive. It is also an all inclusive. I was there as part of a conference. There are many problems, especially for the experienced traveller. The front desk staff, including the manager, were very weak in terms of unserstanding English. This is true throughout the property. Getting an olive in a martini is a chore that takes several requests.The place was 30 per cent full and I was given a room very far from the lobby and the beach. The room was of decent size, but a bit tired. The floors in the halls and rooms are dangerously slippery when wet. The mattress was soft and not comfortable. One very strange thing is that in the standard room there is no solid wall separating the bathroom from the bed room, which limits priivacy .The food, except in the Vento restaurant, was very weak. The steak was horrible and the lobster tails were consistently overdone. The best is the breakfast. At night, look at the fresh fish offerings and have it grilled. Be careful, however, because they tend to overcook everything. I love to snorkel and it is very weak off the beach.  The beach is not bad, but the sand is gritty and there is so much seaweed they have to use a front end loader to remove it. On the plus side, the hotel does provide a  good number of covered chairs and beverage service on the beach. You are not permitted to go on your own to a reef which is in sight. There is a  "free" snorkel which is in a row boat for an hour where you better be good at climbing in and out of boats. There was no ladder. There are excursions that you can pay for. The one they push is for 76.00 on a small cat with no sun coverage. All in all, I was pretty disappointed with the experience.

reviews.author: Bryan F
reviews.title: Good Place over all
reviews.text: I won this trip through work so I started doing research after we had already planned to go.  The one thing that I kept reading was that the "royal service" was well worth the money.  So I decided that I wanted a Ocean Front room and was told that the only way to do that was to do the royal service anyway.  So I did, and without a doubt, it is what made the trip worthwhile.  Having your own pool, bar, towels, beach area, concierge, check in and check out area, snacks any time of day etc.. is well worth the upgrade price.  Jose Ramos in the restaurant area was a real delight.  By the last day he knew what we would be ordering for breakfast and where we liked to sit.  He was great.  The lady at the Illy coffee bar was great also.  The food was better than average for an all-inclusive resort.  I have stayed at a number of them and have never been impressed, but the food here was good enough.  The only thing I did not like was the beach area.  The place where you had chairs and all was good, but the water was not.  There is way too much seaweed in the water.  They even come clean the beach every morning to remove the seaweed but by mid-day its back again.  For this reason I would not go back.  I know that the DR is not the most "Caribbean" place but once again, I won the trip.  I would not spend my own money there though.  The other thing is make sure you get to the airport like 3 hours early.  The place is a mad house!

reviews.author: l0vethebeach87
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort....BUT
reviews.text:
We ended up going to Paradisus as part of a trip I earned through my company.  At first glance, the resort seemed beautiful.   We checked in and the process was easy.  The rooms were very nice and I was happy to have finally arrived.   While waiting for our luggage we checked the stocked mini fridge and I was happy to have two cold beers waiting for me (or so I thought).  I grabbed one of the beers and it just so happened that it was open and half drank.   Yum.  Evidently the people staying before us didnt want to finish that beer.   Anyways, we went down to see the resort and it was very nice, the pools, grounds and ocean were beautiful.   There was a bit of seaweed in the ocean but no big deal, still a very nice beach.   

The big issue I had with this resort was the food.  When you come to an all inclusive, you expect to eat at least decent food.   By no means am I a picky eater who is accustomed to five start luxorious dining, far from it.  In fact, give me Outback Steakhouse and I'm happy so that pretty much puts it in perspective.   The first pain in the neck is even trying to get reservations at the restaurants.   Between them randomly being closed and being forced to make reservations days in advance, it was ridiculous to try to even find a place to eat.   Once you got in the restaurant, the food was average at best.   The only decent meal i had all week was at the hibachi restaurant.   Juan Jose was great cooking for us.   As far as the only other real option for breakfast, lunch, and dinner was the buffet.   Not only was it horrible, it made me sick and I was not able to eat or drink a thing the last two whole days I was there.   What a great way to spend your all inclusive vacation.   I didnt think it was possible to screw up scrambled eggs and bacon...until I came here.   Runny eggs, chewy bacon, no thanks.   I've eaten better food at my high school cafeteria.   I stayed at a 3 star resort in Jamaica last year at the Starfish Trelawny that had much better food.  4 days later and finally home my stomach has finally stopped cramping.   It wasnt just me saying this about the food.   We talked to several other people at the resort about the food and not one had anything good to say about it.  For this reason I would HIGHLY suggest staying elsewhere when choosing a destination to spend your hard earned money.   

The drinks weren't much better unless you were at the lobby bar.   Depending on who made your drinks, they ranged from average to disgusting.  Nothing like a frozen pina colada that's barely frozen.  We even saw a bartender pouring low shelf vodka into an absolut bottle, nice.   

We had no real problem with the service, everyone was pretty pleasant, didnt speak much English but I guess that's to be expected.  

All in all, the weather was nice, resort itself was beautiful but I wouldnt stay here again for free.

reviews.author: willksc
reviews.title: Beautiful resort - A++ service
reviews.text: This is a beautiful resort! My husband won a trip with his company and we stayed 3 nights at this fabulous resort. The food was excellent, the entertainment was great, and the beaches were awesome. The service exceptional! Absolutely would stay here again and again! AND I am a really picky hotel snob!

reviews.author: StPaulCountry_Girl
reviews.title: Best Week Ever!!!
reviews.text: We went to the resort for a week for a work function. There were 90 of us that went coming from all over Canada. The resort was seamless for checkin. We arrived at 10am and had a room ready which was great since check in was 3pm. Our room was so nice and even had bathrobes and slippers. Bar fridge fully stocked was kept full all week. The grounds are breathtaking and spotless. The staff work very hard to pick up everything including cigarette butts. We had a private beach BBQ arranged and it was beautiful and excellent food. I have been to many places and this was the best food I have had hands down. So much variety and it actually tasted really good. Even the desserts!! Drinks were delicious. Top shelf liquor. One of the beach bar waitress's Bianca made us up her special "Dirty Banana" drink that was so yummy.  They even bring you bags of Lays potato chips/Doritos! The bali beds were the only thing we didnt get to enjoy as there were towels on them all very early. I hate the towel game however it is at any resort I have ever been at. You could always find a spot though. We had such a great week here and were impressed constantly throughout the week with the staff and services available. I really wonder about the people putting negative reviews if they just have nothing better to do with their time than complain. You are on vacation.... relax and dont sweat the small stuff!!! :-)

reviews.author: Qflyer
reviews.title: Nice location but overall poor quality
reviews.text:
Just spent 4 days with my wife at the resort.  First time in an all-inclusive, so was very curious to see if it's something i would pay for (I didn't pay for this trip).  The resort itself is not bad - nice beach, decent pool, spread-out.  The food was VERY disappointing - all the restaurants have more-or-less the same food and it's not food that i would pay for in a restaurant.  Nice to be able to get all the drinks and stuff you want, but would have been 100x better if the food was good.  Service was spotty - from housekeeping and on.  One thing that bugged my wife and I was housekeeping just knocked and came in - don't even wait to hear if someone is in the room.  Our A/C was broken when we first checked in, but that was taken care of after I called and talked to someone who could speak English.
Would I pay for this resort myself? Definitely not.  Would I consider staying at a another all-inclusive? Yes, I liked the concept and hope it can be executed better elsewhere.

reviews.author: Willolot
reviews.title: Nice place, shame about the service
reviews.text: Attended our annual sales conference here. Great location on the beach, nice rooms, lovely pool etc. However, they need ti wake up and understand what good service is.Maybe the language barrier is the problem. OK, so I don't speak Spanish, but for such a major hotel catering to the US market the lack of good quality English amongst many of the staff caused real problems. On arrival my wife wanted to take a bath. The plug did not fit properly, so she rang reception to ask for it to be fixed, so that the water would stay in the bath. The sent a man to fix the toilet! We were supposed to have wired internet in the rooms. There were at least 4 RJ45 ports on the wall. None of them worked. I reported this at least 3 times to reception and nothing was done about it. The restaurants on site were good, bit if you did not book before 4pm you were not allowed in, even if they were empty (which they usually were). We arrived at 5pm on our first day and had to eat in the buffet.  We ended up with so many of us at our conference booking tables of 8 in restaurants and then deciding where we would go, but what a pain. It would be so much easier to just turn up. I was working all day and my wife wanted to relax, so why did we have to plan so much each day where we would eat. It all seemed to petty.

reviews.author: M'times
reviews.title: Meet All Expectations
reviews.text:
2nd time at this resort and 4th time to Punta Cana and would say this resort offers everything you need. Great rooms, clean beach with plenty of chairs, decent golf course included in package and  other high end courses close. Food in restaurants better than average
Hard to beat the Paradisus as a chain (have stayed in their resorts in Mexico , Costa Rica and Puerto Rico also)
Staff was excellent and service (especially at the beach bar) was very good.
yes you can find cheaper resorts but  the extra paid is worth it to know you will have a quality resort.

reviews.author: Mar154980
reviews.title: This was just about Paradise
reviews.text:
We had booked into this hotel as a result of a business conference and might never have selected it otherwise.  We have been to many islands and the Dominican wasn't really on our list.  But we have changed our minds.  It was beautiful!   The conference was 4 days and we extended it to 6 to have a bit more time there.

We have always felt that when you are dealing with an all-inclusive resort, you can't expect the meals to be outstanding.  This was the case at the Paradisus.  Some things were a bit bland, others overdone, but some were very very good.

You had your choice of about 3 or 4 of the restaurants--the Vento, the Passion, the Bano and the Market Grill.  There was also the Naos which was open for breakfast, lunch and dinner whereas the Passion and the Vento were just for dinner.  We ate once at the Passion, once at Vento, quite a bit at Naos and did not eat at all at the Market Grill or Bano so cannot comment on them.  The other meals were with the conference, outside on the beach and were good.  Certainly, there were numerous choices of food, including seafood, meats and poultry.  

What we did find interesting and also disappointing was that there were vegetables served for breakfast and lunch at Naos but when you went to the fancier restaurants, there were no vegetables.  I remember having a Grouper dish at Passion and it was excellent, but that's all that was on the plate--no veggies.  You did get a salad or soup before, but no substantial vegetables other than sometimes potato.  I think the desserts were probably the least favourable item on the whole.  Most of the banana bread type things or consistencies were too heavy.  At lunch, though, we enjoyed a variety of parfaits--they were light, frothy and yes, sugary.  You will get lots of sugar on the whole.

On the beach, the service was great for drinks, etc.  The girls would come around and take your order, or you could go yourself to the swim-up-bar or the regular bar all near the pool area.  The drinks varied at first--I remember ordering a strawberry daquari which tasted anything but like a strawberry daquari--it was pure sugar and no real strawberries.  But after that we got familiar with the good ones, including a mud slide, a Banana Mama and "Victor Happy".  There is a bartender named Victor at the swim-up-bar who named this last drink--a mixture of rum, orange, pineapple and banana.  I don't know whether they were the juices of those fruits or whole pieces.  But it is yummy if you like the frothy drinks which I do.  The girls would often come back with an extra drink for you and, of course, if you tip them, they will continue to do that.  But it is worth it for what they do.  We also had a few drinks at the other bar where "Fuego Fuego" is.  I see he has been mentioned here before.  He sings those words but I think his real name is Migel.  Very funny, very enjoyable--later in the day you can see him pouring drinks from way up in the air down into someone's throat!!  It is well worth tipping these people.

We are dance enthusiasts and so were very happy to go to our daily class near the pool once in the a.m. and once in the p.m.   Here we met Jimmy at first, but only for a day or two.  Then Jose took over for most of the rest of our trip.  These guys are great and absolutely helped to make our trip more enjoyable.  Jose had all his hilarious Spanish expressions (which were half English) so you knew what he was saying. We not only learned some new dance steps, but were highly entertained as well.  Of course I ended up dancing with Jose at night as well, as there was a band most nights that played Latin music to dance to and we were there quite a few nights.  The dancing and Jose were one of my highlights  of this whole trip.  By the way, the Bands that did play were excellent!!  The entertainment, in general, was typical for a hotel.  It was good, but not quite professional.  Just a note on the dance scene--there was a lot of confusion for us as to where we could go to dance outside of the hotel.  The tour guides only had 1 place to suggest called "Imagine" and otherwise they could not recommend anything else that was safe.  But Imagine didn't open til midnight and if you took their tour, they'd pick you up at 4:00 a.m.  We felt this was much too late for a couple of middle-age people.  Then we spoke to the concierge who said there were definitely a couple of other places, one of which was the Mangoo and La Punta and that they were also safe.  It wasn't clear whether Imagine was being pushed because it was through the hotel or whether or not they truly felt it was the only one they could recommend.   The concierge told us that Mangoo opened at l0:00 and dancing started at ll:00 but when we finally decided we were going to try one of these places, the guy who orders the taxis for you said the dancing wouldn't really start til midnight also and that you couldn't get in early.  At that point we gave up and stayed at the hotel.  My feeling was that no one really knew exactly  what was going on in terms of these dance clubs.  For those of you who love to dance, I'd just speak to the guy who orders the taxis--he knows!!

My husband tried one of the sailboats one day and was a bit disappointed as he sensed that  they had made the boat "slow down" for safety.  He said there was enough wind that the boat should have been going faster.  Perhaps they've had some smart alecs who have caused problems in the past.

The weather on the whole was fabulous.  One day or two where it was cloudy and rainy all morning and then suddenly by noon, clear skies, sunny and gorgeous.  The sand was cool to the touch as was the walking area around the pool.

A lot of the staff did not speak much English at all and so they had to find someone else who did often.  If you can learn some basics in Spanish, it goes a long way.  Although I found that when they did speak English, they kept saying to me that I didn't need to try and speak Spanish, almost as if it was a waste of their time.  But I told one person at the Towel Bar that I wanted to say my room number in Spanish and so he was cool with that.

This is a beautiful hotel with beautful views out to the sea from inside.  We did not get an ocean view from our room, but it didn't matter--we were  hardly in our rooms.  There is one small area off the main floor where they have some flamingoes in a pond.  Try to catch this just at dusk as well as during the day.  It has to be one of the most tranquil spots I've ever seen.  When it's getting dark, all you see are the pink colours of the flamingoes against the dark sky--so pretty and peaceful.

We had some minor issues with the hair dryer not working on the first day there, but since I always bring my own anyway,  we didn't care.  Otherwise the service in the rooms was excellent.  I think one time they forgot to come and change the towels, but I saw one of the maids on our floor and she brought some over immediately.  The people here are on the whole very friendly.  I think that when they do not speak English, they are obviously 
less talkative.  But again, if you say a few words in Spanish, they appreciate it.

The one other thing I found unusual concerned setting up a credit account at the front desk.  We did that after a few days as a convenience and that part was fine.  But if you do that, they don't bother giving you a receipt at the little shopping store there.  They say that you'll get your receipt on your bill itemizing everything.  When we were checking out the night before we left, they had put our bill under the door, but it only showed the total amount spent in Dominican money, and did not show the items purchased.  We knew what we had bought and approximately what it would be in our money, so with a little calculation, we could figure it out.  But if you had bought a ton of stuff, not getting a receipt initially, you'd have a hard time without it being itemized.  I explained this to someone at the front desk and suggested that  perhaps they should put the amount in 
U. S. dollars as well.  He didn't seem very interested and made no comment.

One of the neatest things they had were like square beds dotted along the path to the beach and around the pool.  They were covered and  had a mattress of some sort and you could just sleep, read or whatever there with no sun.  If you wanted the sun, you could put a chair or two in front of it.  But you have to get up real early to put your towels down on it to indicate it's yours.  We wanted to try them, but were not going to get up before 7:00 a.m.!!

All in all, we were very happy with our stay at this hotel and would definitely recommend it.

reviews.author: Jaume67
reviews.title: fantastico
reviews.text:
El mejor hotel en el que me he alojado.Trato excelente,gran servicio en real service.
Felicidades Bernard Wiss,,tienes un equipo de trabajo excelente.

reviews.author: JJH7882
reviews.title: Phenomenal Experience!  Fantastic Staff!
reviews.text: An excellent venue for hosting a conference with plenty of opportunities to enjoy the amenities.  The entire staff went out of their way to make my stay first class!  Could not have asked for a nicer experience.

reviews.author: EESSMM
reviews.title: Great place !!!!
reviews.text: Amazing food, incredible rooms, great beach... You need to be here !!!

reviews.author: ToophDoctor
reviews.title: Worth every cent!
reviews.text: The room was beautiful. Service was superb. Food was very good.  Drinks were top shelf.  Night life on the resort was not very lively but I was there to relax so I didn't mind.  As a matter of fact, I never left the resort between arrival and departure. I stayed on the Royal Service side so the butler and adults only pool/beach  was very nice. I will definitely be returning again.

reviews.author: DeepDivr
reviews.title: Wonderful Hotel - Wonderful Service
reviews.text: Stayed at the Paradisus for 4 nights.  The hotel was decided for us as the purpose of the trip was business.   Prior to leaving, I read the many mixed reviews on TA and got to the hotel with a small bit of hesitation.   Boy...was I pleasantly surprised.  Lobby area was fabulous.  While my only criticism was the time required to check in and check out, it wasn't as bad as some other locations I've visited.  Very friendly and helpful.  Got my room and was taken to my room in an building about 100 yards away.  Very nice grounds.  The room was amazing.  I was traveling by myself and really didn't need much but was greeted by a huge room with sitting area, very comfortable king bed, 2 person jacuzzi tub, separate large shower with multiple shower heads and a big flat screen TV.  Not that TV was high on the priorities, but it did give me a chance to keep up with the news back home.   Beautiful pool, friendly and efficient bar staff, good food at the two restaurants I took advantage of and a beautiful beach.  All was in great repair, clean and all well attended to.   No one hassled me about time shares...not once.  Did not encounter an unfriendly staff member or ran into any situation that didn't meet a very  high expectation.   Not sure what happend to those who wrote negative reviews.   Fortunately, I couldn't find anything to complain about.   Nothing missing from my room, very friendly, attentive service...all in all a very nice place.  Is it a 5 Star hotel?  Probably not.  Is it a strong 4 Star....yes.  If you go with reasonable expectations, I can't imagine you would be disappointed.  I'm sure the price you pay will determine what you expect.  I had a very reasonable group rate and got far more than my money's worth.   Good luck and enjoy.

reviews.author: Jennyfer74
reviews.title: Perfect place
reviews.text:
I have to say, I was a little hesitant about staying here after reading some of the reviews on this site. I am very picky and have a little tolerance for bad service. But thankfully my fears were completely unfounded. High standard and good value.
Every request made to the front desk or our group manager was met with a big smile and an "no problemo, ahora mismo" response. I called for various minor things , never had to wait more than 10 minute for "problem" solution.
The rooms were clean and big, with very nice view. I had a view on little pool with flamingo's walking around ,really nice to see.
Use their business center for checking emails instead of the in-room internet service which is cumbersome to use and much more expensive since you have to pay a flat rate for 24 hours vs the business center PC use - you only pay for the time you are on the computer, tickets with minutes that can be used over few days. Telephone rent deal is good, too, cheaper than any deal from hotel and roaming adventures wit overpriced bills.
The pool area is very nice, I had a swim every morning. Hotel has some lovely features , amazing fountains, incredible beautiful beach, with live dj show at the weekend, directly on the beach, ...I didn't even want to leave the hotel at night because of its great restaurants and bars, and Gabi Beach Lounge area is excellent.
didn't speak much Spanish, and there was always someone to help me in English, very nice people and staff. Food was good, breakfast just how I like -  a lot of fruit yogurt, fresh fruit plates, croissants, cereal, honey,etc.
I would definitely stay there again. Slightly priced but compared to other places I think it was worth it.

reviews.author: c0reyann
reviews.title: Loved the views, hated the food
reviews.text:
I somewhat wish that I had read up on the reviews for this resort before traveling here for business (photographer for a wedding at the resort) but in a way I'm glad that I didn't because I didn't go in with any preconceived ideas of what it would be like.  

Check In:  
Check in was pretty easy, we were able to get a room right away, but there were a lot of people lounging in the lobby and it was easy to tell that they had been waiting a long time.  There was definitely some issues with the language barrier as neither of us spoke a whit of Spanish.  

Room:
Since we were there for work (and the room was paid for by the bride and groom) we had the cheapest room on the resort.  It was laid out in the typical hotel room standard with island flare.  The room was cool and we had no issues at all with air conditioning - but we heard from others in the group that wasn't always the case in the rooms.  Also I have to make note of the bathrooms - there are just some wooden blinds with lots of open spaces between the bathroom and the rest of the room.  You can see and hear EVERYTHING that goes on in there - if you are remotely shy, it may be a disaster for you!  

Service:
While we had to ask for some beverages at mealtimes a few times, I never was bothered by it.  There was definitely a language barrier at times but nothing that ever completely frustrated me.  While we only had one day to enjoy the beach/pool, I wasn't bothered by the fact that there wasn't waiters wandering around getting me drinks - I was fine going to the bar myself for it. Housekeeping was efficient and the only thing that annoyed me with them is that they would show up early - often at 8AM or so - for service in the morning.  Room service was always quick- 30 minutes or so - and accurate. 

Food & Drink:
Here's where my beef is, the food was TERRIBLE in my opinion.  By far the best meal of the stay was the reception food at the wedding.  Since we didn't have Royal Service, VIP, Vacation Club or any of the other special services, we were stuck with eating at Naos for most of our meals and to say the food was lacking there is being generous.  I never thought of myself as an overly picky eater until this trip.  We were able to get one reservation for the trip at Vento and while some of the food was good, the filet was awful.  Very tough and overcooked.  They also didn't bring out a steak knife and cutting that tough meat with a butter knife was a joke.  The Market Grill was never open so we weren't able to try that as a secondary option.  Room service was okay - better than the buffet for sure.  Just overall though it was hard for me to find food I liked and enjoyed (I don't like seafood).  I hear that the food for the more elite services (Reserver, VIP, Royal Service) was better though.  I heard later that there were a few people who got sick in the wedding group from one of the restaurants.  The drinks were good and weren't hard to find - the lounge bar was probably one of the better ones to hit up for a drink compared to the others. 

Resort:
The resort is beautiful.  Perfect landscaping, beautiful pools and stunning beaches.  It really was a visual paradise.  Definitely one of the nicest pools that I've been to - and remember, I was in the normal pools.  The fancier service pools looked even nicer.  The beach area was nice and our first day there we didn't know any better and ended up in the Royal Service area of the beach on one of the mattresses and weren't kicked off.  I have to say, those are really really nice!!!  The one day that we had to enjoy the resort I do have to say it wasn't easy finding a chair but it wasn't impossible.  

Wedding:
I can't review the wedding from a guest or bridal party viewpoint but from a vendor viewpoint the wedding was perfect.  The ceremony location on the beach was stunning and by far one of the most beautiful locations I've seen on the beach (right between two palm trees).  The reception was set up on Gabi Beach and was also beautiful and perfect for a destination wedding.  The food was really good - the best meal of the trip for me.  A lot of why the wedding was so amazing was because the couple were simply amazing but the resort did set the frame for a perfect day.  

Overall it wasn't a BAD experience, but just wasn't one I came home raving about.  If hired again to go there, I would in a heartbeat and wouldn't be upset about it but I can't say that it is a place that I would choose to return to for a relaxing vacation.

reviews.author: NCFlyFisher25
reviews.title: Best for Sales Club Trip
reviews.text:
I've taken my group of 30-40 people (sales club winners) all over the Carribbean (jamaica, Mexico, St. Thomas, St. John) and this was their favorite hotel.    The hotel is beautiful and although the staff speaks very little English, we found it to be a great place.  The ladies said this had the best Spa of all we've been to.  The all inclusive inclulded everything including horse back riding!  And the food was quite good.  

The cabanas with the large king sized mattresses arranged all over the resort are hpynotic -- especially the ones near the fountains.

reviews.author: canadabanada
reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.text:
Stayed here for a week at the begining of this month. The rooms were beautiful, people were lovely. Food was good. Great service to the rooms for food. One morning a gardener climbed a palm tree to get coconuts for us then opened them and sliced the meat out for us. he was so nice!
      Everything you could want is here. My only tiny complaint was trying to get coffee or drinks while in the restaurants. coffee service was odd and hard to get unless we ordered it to our room . The espresso bar was not open early in the morning either which was odd.
    The gym is small with only 3 treadmills so I took to running barefoot on the beach which was superb. The auqafit instructor was a bonus.. 
      Keep your valuables locked in the safe though, a couple of my co workers got some jewelry stolen but we left stuff out all over our room and had no issues. 
  We tipped 1-2$ a day for housekeeping and some for turn down service. We tipped a lot of people they seemed to appreciate it a lot.
   The pools were lovely, everywhere was kept VERY clean too. Beach is awesome here.
  Sushi was delicious and well worth going to, I recommend the volcano sushi dish, they light it on fire when they serve it to you.
   The spa was wonderous, with hydrotherapy pools you can use prior to any treatments.
I had a wrap and massage on my first day, then on the last day we checked out, used the beach and pools then went to the spa, where we used the therapy pools, outdoor showers, had a pedicure and got ready for our trip home. It was a perfect way to end our stay. Better than the hospitality room on the last day.
   The music on dancing nights was fun and we danced the night away a couple times.
The staff does a great job. Thank you.
oh PS.. the beds were very comfy !

reviews.author: michaelaurasmom
reviews.title: Beautiful resort & beach, but not up to "Leading Hotels of the World" stature
reviews.text: This is a gorgeous resort, but they are behind on service, particularly with it's 5 star rating.  Punta Cana itself is a beautiful place, but one should not have to brush their teeth with bottled water in this day and age.   We paid for the "Royal Service" which entitles you to a butler, whom I never met in the 6 nights we were there.  Food is adequate.  This place has great potential, but not there yet.

reviews.author: WarrenA
reviews.title: Site inspection
reviews.text: We stayed in The Reserve one bedroom suites. Great rooms,Great food & Great facilities. Lots of walking & a little trouble being understood. I'll brush up on my Spanish for next time. Small casino, and not real crowded last week. Had fun on 2 VIP tours.

reviews.author: ElisaAH
reviews.title: Mejor todo incluido de Lujo
reviews.text: Para disfrutar un buen vino y una langosta a la orilla de la playa.

reviews.author: GaTraveler1950
reviews.title: Pretty place but food and service are very mediocre
reviews.text: This resort is in a beautiful spot, with nice wide and long beaches.  The resort is very large, and it can take you 5 minutes or so to walk from your room to the beach.  The resort's architectural design is very good, and it makes a great first impression. Our room, however, was musty, and after cleaning it smelled as though oven cleaner had been used as a disinfectant.  The food in the buffet restaurants is not good at all--the food in the speciality restaurants is better--but they are hard to reserve--it seems there are not nearly enough tables there to accommodate the size of the resort..  The staff can at times be very nice, and at other times rude.  You can understand why--they are subjected to large groups of people who demand prompt and attentive service and who, it seems for the most part, don't tip or otherwise express their appreciation for good service.  If you think of this as a land-locked cruise ship, and one that is at the low end of the quality scale, you will be just about on point.

reviews.author: Lespaulmojo
reviews.title: Very nice inclusive resort.
reviews.text:
First of all, this is an all-inclusive hotel.  If you are looking for a great food experience, or lot's of choices, etc, don't go; it's like most  cruises.  The included wine is pretty weak and beer is Presidente, but some of the bars have Heineken and Bud, nut nothing fancier.  The normal liqueurs are quite acceptable, however.  The buffet has great fruit and typically a good breakfast; have them make you an omelet.  

As for some of the other reviews, there is simply some misinformation.  Yes, the hotel staff isn't highly fluent in English but if you speak slowly, they get it and they work hard to remember what you like.  Bring lots of ones ($1), again, it's like a cruise, they're working for tips.  The pool staff is great, tip a little and they will almost have your drink ready next time before you ask.  And no, the reason someone didn't have towels, is they didn't ask to find you walk all of 20 yds to the towel cabana...  And, FYI, the pools are great.   Yes, it is very hot and humid here, but the AC in the rooms works very well.  Our group was very large and I know of know complaints.  The hotel is also very clean.  Tip your maid $5 on first day and your room will be even more so during your whole stay.  Safes have combinations and are standard sturdy units, so a theft should be rare, but they did seem to open if there was a power failure.  As a side, this happened to one of our group and the maid left a note that the safe was open and she was leaving the room until the guests returned, nothing was missing.  The beach is quite nice and again, misinformation, a group of men in green jumpsuits cleans up the seaweed very early every morning.  It returns a little during the day but is soft and won't effect your beach enjoyment.  There are numerous extra curricular beach activities available as well.
Also, room service was reasonably fast and was very acceptable.

Life is tough for the average resident of this country.  Working here is a chance to do better.  They work very hard to please you if you only let them.  Learn a dozen Spanish words, smile, be friendly, and tip fairly.  Do that and you will have a good time.

Too sum it up, would I pay to go here, no, but neither would I pay to go on a cruise.  But as a place for a group to have a big event, it's more than fine.

reviews.author: Toutpartout
reviews.title: Resort life at its best
reviews.text:
Travelled  to Punta Cana here for a conference . Stayed at the Pariadisus Palma Real which is one of 3 hotels on the compound. 

Resort is expansive, alot to do, no real need to venture outside. THere is literally everything onsite. 

There is even a mall near the exit but within the hotel compund to keep you shopping- good souvenir shops , even a cinema but the clothing stores are brand names which are much more expensive than in the USA- so don't bother buying brand names
Rooms are impeccable, food supply unending, staff very friendly, pool and beaches , gym and  landscaping  amazing.

Conference rooms  well-equipped. 

What more can I say except I never left the compound- there was literally everything on site. Had no experience of the local culture which was a bit sad but such is resort life!

Multiple restaurants, multiple pools, beware of the 15 USD charge to use the internet at the business centre and in your room.

Excellent hotel overall and the hotel photographer is excellent- really!

reviews.author: CRS2001
reviews.title: Work paid so that is the saving grace of this trip.
reviews.text:
First off, I will say that this place is absolutely beautiful when you get in there.  There are fountains all over, the restaurants are beautiful, and even the furniture is top notch.  The golf course was gorgeous as well and very reasonably priced.  Sound good?  Well, back up.

One of the biggest problems I had with this place was the service.  Hardly anyone speaks solid English and there is no place to exchange money other than the casino.  Then you think maybe you can go swim in the ocean and take a break.  But when you get there, there is seaweed everywhere and apparently the idea of having someone sweep it out every day has not hit this place yet.  Service at the pool bar stinks and for a place that is supposed to have areas for kids and adults respectively, it sure seemed like there were kids everywhere.  Now kids are great, but not when you leave home to get a break from them.  Oh, and no infiniti pool.

Basically, the people are either moronic or rude.  Neither of which I appreciate.  So I would recommend that if you are going to spend this kind of money on a 5 star resort, go to a Sandals in Jamaica....

reviews.author: RoadWarrior-FL
reviews.title: Nice, but wouldn't do again.
reviews.text:
I was here for three nights with a group and have to say, all of the reviews are about right.  This is a hotel with breathtaking features, a great stretch of beach, and immaculate grounds.  It also has very hit and miss service and awful food.

First thing, when you get to the airport, prepare for an onslaught of people offering to help you.  We chose a car service in advance, and if you are making your first trip, this is advisable.  Now that I know the deal, would probably just cab it, but the first time can be a little tough.

We arrived and the check-in process was smooth.  Our room, like 95% of the rooms, overlooked a garden.  We were not in the concierge area.  The room was clean, though looked worn in places  It was very humid---a theme that recurred in our room and every room in our group all three nights.  It was so humid that the sheets were damp.  We later learned that the AC turns off in the room when you leave due to motion sensors (which means it also shuts off at night when sleeping)---but if you leave your fan on, it leaves the AC on.  I had to keep it around 58-60 on the thermostat to keep it cool, due to the dampness.

The service was hit and miss.  Some people were very helpful, some where unhelpful.  We never could get room service to answer the phone and there were never towels by the pool, but we found getting drinks and other help very easy.  It is not an easy place if you don't know any Spanish, but if you can hack through a couple dozen words and phrases, you will be fine.  We also found room service hit and miss.  Sometimes our room was immaculate, sometimes they didn't even tuck in the sheets or pick up all the towels.  The amount of tip seemed to have no bearing. 

The food here was awful.  This was the biggest downfall.  The buffet was atrocious.  The running joke in our group was this place was a weight loss facility.  They could screw up the easiest things, like corn and potatoes.  We ate one night at Passion, which was decent and one at Gabi Beach, which was very good---but it comes with a bill.  One in my group compared the sushi restaurant to eating shoes.  For the price, the food should be better.

I played golf at the course across the street.  It was a nice layout, fairly challenging and well maintained.  The shuttle runs on a "schedule," unless you pay the driver (who just hangs in the parking lot) to take you the 1/4 mile back to the resort.    If you play golf, it is a fun course.  One thing- do stock up on bottled water before you start playing as there is no cart service on the course.

The pools are great.  The beach is great (there is a nice little art market down the beach) and the people mostly were great.  But the food was  inedible and the service was sketchy enough that for the price, I would not make a return visit.

reviews.author: junoman973
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, Very Poor Service.
reviews.text:
This has been my second trip to the Palma Real. My group was really lucky to get upgraded to Royal service which allowed us to get lunch at the reserve and stay over at the palma real hotel. The service everywhere was really bad.. My group is all from New York City and is very use to tipping to get good service, this didnt even help. Servers would say i will bring something and disappear and never return and at breakfest it was the most noticeable.
The hotel needs to have someone take each area of the hotel and try to improve service. This hotel is not cheap, and honestly i really think if you are spending this type of money go to the Rivera maya, like Royal Hideaway or Grand Velas. The property is very beautiful and i really like the nightlife they had each evening. The food was fine. The other issue was trying to get reservations, they were either 6pm or 945pm, it became a project to get dinner reservations. I noticied the people who were club share owners were able to get any time they wanted while the hotel guests were given what was left. The spa was nice but also needed some imporvements. If you get a good rate at property go for it, if you looking for something really special, again look at rivera maya in mexico..

reviews.author: OntarioHeatseeker
reviews.title: Great Location
reviews.text:
Attended a convention at the Paridisus mid Feb. We were upgraded to the Royal Service. We have stayed at the Paradisus in Mexico, Costa Rica and Puerto Rico and all have great  grounds and rooms. The rooms are well appointed and were serviced twice a day.
BIggest complaint would be service  the buffet restaurants. Food was so so but the service was terrible. 3 mornings we never did get coffee. 
The speciality restaurants at night had good food and service and the waiters at the Royal Service pool were great. They went out of there way to look after you.
They just opened a new complex (The Reserve) which is family oriented and has a great pool system. It is not on the beach but shuttles will bring you on a regular schedule
Unlimited golf (cart fee only) is included at the Cocotel course (27 holes across the street from resort) Course is decent but pace of play is ridiculus. 5-6 hour rounds were the norm for the week. The course is not owned by the hotel but this should be addressed. We did go to the Le Cana course at the Punta Cana Resort (about 25 minute drive from paradisus) which is a spectacular course. Has 4 holes that border the ocean so don't forget your camera. ($165 US a round)
The  ever present Dominican wind keeps the temperature bearable but there are some days you would get sandblasted on the beach so the pool was a welcome retreat.
Overall the grounds , beach and quality of your room make this a very enjoyable place to visit.

reviews.author: tamlyn63
reviews.title: Great vacation destination!
reviews.text:
My husband, our 15 yr daughter, 13 yr son and I stayed at the Paradisus Jan 15th- 20th 2009.  This was an annual  incentive trip through one of our business vendors.  We payed extra to bring our children along with us this year. Besides us, our group totalled around 250-300 people.  Some people chose to upgrade to the Royal Service or Family Concierge.  We did not. 

First I'd like to mention that I spend 6 months or longer researching each destination the trip is at prior to the departure date so I'm somewhat familiar with what;s offered on and off resort before we go.  We are in the middle income bracket, very laid back and prefer casual living, not the sort who expect to be waited on hand and foot but do appreciate a little pampering, and definately not food snobs but do enjoy a good meal. With that said, I'm somewhat astounded by all the negative reviews this resort has received.  We had an outstanding vacation and I would not hesitate to stay at this resort again.

Day 1:
Travel day.  Up at 4am to board our 6am flight from St Louis to Miami.  2 hr layover then board our 12 noon flight to Punta Cana and arrive at 3:20pm.  We were provided with the $11 ticket to enter the country and went right through customs to get our bags and board the buses to the resort.  Arrived at the resort, checked in at the hospitality desk our vendor had set up and was shown to our room where our luggage had already been delivered.  Walked around the resort to get a feel of the layout and then had dinner at the buffet.  Finished off the night at the Gabi Beach Bar where they had a fire dancer show.

Day 2: 
 Breakfast at the buffet, then spent the rest of the day between the beach and the pool with a lunch break at the buffet. We also walked the beach and bought a few souveniers from some of the beach vendor "malls", I'd guess you'd call them. Dinner was a welcome reception in the ballroom put on by our business vendor with more firedancers and a band for entertainment.  Then it was back to the Gbai Beach Bar followed by dancing in the disco.  

Day3 :
Buffet breakfast, then to the beach to watch/participate in the Beach Olympics our business vendor had organized for our group.  Hubby and I watched, our kids participated.  Again the day was spent on the beach or by the pool.  Dinner at the buffet and back to Gabi Beach bar for the evening

Day4:
Got up early to get my son to the lobby to meet the rest of his foursome for a round of golf at Cocotal.  The rest of us breakfasted at the buffet, lounged on the beach and at the pool.  Upon my son's return and after a late lunch, we met in the lobby with people from our group to do the Segway excursion.  After that, back to the pool til dinner time and our usual Gabi Beach Bar.

Day 5:
Beakfast at the buffet, then off to Bavaro Splash where the 4 of us went on the speed boat (2 persons per boat) and snorkel excursion.  After that my son and I did the parasailing through the same watersport vendor.  Dinner was a Farewell reception in the ballroom through our business vendor.

Day 6:
Departure day.  We had the buffet for breakfast and were on a bus to the airport by 11am to catch our flight via Puerto Rico to St Thomas where we stayed another 5 days at the Frenchmans Reef Marriott.  I'll post that review there if anyone's interested.

The Resort:
The grounds are beautifully landscaped and meticulously maintained.  It is rather large and sprawled out, so be prepared to do a lot of walking.

The Rooms:
Our room was large and clean.  I saw no disrepair, mold or mildew that has been reported in some reviews.  We did not upgrade, so our room was a garden view, but we spent very little time in the room anyway, so who cares?  Some of our business collegues upgraded to Royal Service.  Their room was not any larger, but did have an oustanding view of the pool areas and the beach.

The Resort staff and service:
I have to say of all the Caribbean Islands we've visited so far, this resort had THE friendliest and most accomodating staff I've ever experienced. Not just the bartenders and the wait staff, but the groundskeepers and housekeeping as well.  I read a review of someone complaining how their fridge in their room didn't have enough drinks in it.  Well, our $5 a day tip left in the fridge with a note insured that not only was our fridge STUFFED to capacity with Presidente and water, but he took away the drinks we didn't like and brought us the stuff we wanted.  Every day, we had an 8 pk of beer, 4 7ups, 4 pepsis, 4 diet cokes, and 6 waters.  Then he'd leave a couple more of each on the table(warm) to add to the fridge as wee needed throughtout the day.  I know some people think all inclusive means you don't have to tip, but a dollar or two here and there can make a big difference in how you get treated.  Treat people rude and like servants/slaves then don't expect smiles and politeness from them, let alone enthusiam.  Our favorite bartender at Gabi Beach Bar, Neftali, says he makes $320.00 a month.  He knew us by name after our first night there, greeted us by name every day thereafter.  And we never had to ask for a drink, had another one in front of us before the one we were drinking was gone.  We probably tipped him $5-10 throughtout the day each day.  Same with Joaquin and Rosario at the pool/beach.  On the beach Rosario would find us, we never had to look for her.  $5 a day to housekeeping got us extra towels and toiletries every day.  Just saying, treat people courteously and with respect and you'll recieve the same.  And as far as the language barrier I've heard some complaints about, HELLO, you're in another country and english is not their native toungue.  I never found it to be a problem.

The beach: 
What's  there to say but FABULOUS!  Again I read some negative reviews about the seagrass and trash on the beach.  We saw workers every day pre-dawn raking up the seagrass and picking up trash.  By the end of the day the seagrass is back because, HELLO, where do you think it comes from?  As far as trash goes, the worst is in the "no man's land" between the resorts where  the locals "set up shop".  That's to be expected but even so it wasn't that bad except for one area that I saw.  Now for trash on the beach of the resort, then I'd say point your fingers at the slobs who left it in the first place, you know who you are.

The Food:
As I said before, we are not food snobs but do appreciate good food.  Other than the Welcome and Farewell receptions in the ballroom, we ate every meal at the buffet and a couple late night burgers and fries from room service.  I'd have to say, in conflict to some of the reviews I've read, that the food was above average.  The variety of food on the buffets were numerous and if you left unsatisfied, it's your own fault!  The only dishes I did not like were a few new things I tried that weren't bad, just not to my taste.  We did not go to any of the specialty restaurants just because we were taking advantage of all the beach time we could and did not feel like taking the time to get "dressed up" for dinner.  Like I said we're casual and laid back.   Some in our business group tried all the specialty restaurants and I heard all of the restaurants were very good. The Welcome reception was a casual affair, buffet style, and they pulled out all the stops-king crab legs, ceviche, grilled jumbo shrimp, pork loin, prime rib, lobster tail, etc., etc. etc., very high end food and probably the best meal of our stay.  The Farewell reception was a more formal sit down with filet mignon and lobster tail and was very good also.

Activities and excursions:
If you're not into just relaxing by the pool or on the beach, there's numerous things to do.  I highly recommend the Segway-$40 pp for 1 hr or 70pp for 2 hr.  My son played golf for free but he did have to rent clubs and buy golf balls.  I think his clubs were $60.  The Bavaro Splash speedboat/snorkel was 135.00 per boat so $270 for the 4 of us.  My son and I parasailed for $85 for the two of us.  We saw a "flying dingy"  a dingy attached to a hangglider that literally flies.  We talked to a man who went on it, $60.  He said it was great.  One thing I have to mention, the day before we went on the speedboats, a lady had flipped one from hitting waves or a reef.  They can be dangerous, the boat my daughter and I had, had a sticky throttle and getting it unstuck to slow down was tricky.  I made sure they knew about it afterwards.  There were many excursions that I would like to haven taken but time constraints to and from the resort, aside from the length of our stay prevented us from doing them.  All the more reason to return.  

Overall our experience at this resort was awesome and I would definitely go again.  The ONLY negative thing I could find to say about the trip is the beach vendors can be a little pushy.  We found a simple " no thanks" usually worked.  The other thing would be the conditions "off resort".  Pretty primitive in many areas and makes you realize it is 3rd world.  Please feel free to email me with any questions or comments.  Below is a link to oour pics, including the ones from St Thomas.  Let me know if it won't open.  Will post videos after I've got them edited.

 http://www.shutterfly.com/lightbox/view.sfly?fid=1e3ffba62d571c926cbbd47cbb382743

reviews.author: John B
reviews.title: Quite odd but a beautiful property
reviews.text: As an American traveler this place just might drive you a little crazy. It is a beautiful property with a first class beach, beautiful sand and warm water. The processes and procedures are at best confusing and at worst devious. Eat in the cafeteria as the reservation restuarant scene is an exercise in frustration and quite honestly did not have very good food. There were quite a few individuals in our group including myself who developed some stomach issues which I assume were food related. Clearly the resort caters to travelers from Spain and I can't speak for their needs and wants but we were a bit underwhelmed by the sevice and the food. Our room was very nice and clean and for the most part up to date, no issues there. As I mentioned earlier the property was excellent, well maintained and on a fantastic beach. On balance this place needs some better management and is wasting a wonderful asset. We stayed at the Paradisus in Costa Rica a few years ago and enjoyed our stay and the Country much better.

reviews.author: dnllmz
reviews.title: My Palma Real Wedding
reviews.text:
Sorry this really long and mostly all wedding related. I stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real from Nov 1, 2008 to Nov 10, 2008 our wedding was on Nov 6th.  Derek and I went a couple of days early.  Most of our guests stayed from November 3rd to November 10th.  We did have a couple of guests come for only 4 or 5 days and each one were disappointed they didn’t book for a longer stay.  We had a total of 28 guests and 1 infant.  It was the most beautiful resort I’ve ever been to.  All of my worrying about whether or not I’d picked the right resort to have my wedding at was unnecessary, I made the right decision.  There were a couple of hiccups but nothing major.  Everything was fixed.  I

Airlines:  We flew US Airways on the way in.  We checked in 4 bags and were only charged the $50 overweight fee.  We carried on one bag and my dress.  They did have a closet to hang my dress in but the flight attendant recommended I fold my dress in half and stick it in the overhead bin because she thought the closet would bunch the bottom of my dress up and it would be more wrinkled that way.  So I folded it in the overhead and luckily everyone was nice enough not to put anything in the overhead I had it in.  It was a full flight too.  So the whole plane ride I was a nervous wreck about my dress, actually I was a nervous wreck about my dress the moment we stepped in to the Philly airport and had to go through security.  But my dress was fine!!!  The Palma Real cannot steam your dress for you, I brought a hand steamer but luckily I didn’t need it for my dress.  

On the way home we flew US 3000.  We checked in 3 bags and were charged $25 for one being overweight and $25 for an extra baggage.  We were happy with the $50 each way, we expected to pay more.  And we carried on two bags.  We packed my dress in the bag that had the wedding favors since it was empty now.
